current.name: NVIDIA
current.utility: NVIDIA designs and sells accelerated‑computing GPUs and related software that power AI model training, inference and high‑performance data‑center workloads; its primary users are cloud service providers, large enterprises and research institutions that run AI and scientific computing workloads.
evidence: Data Center revenue of $30.8 billion in the nine‑month period ended Oct 27 2024, driven by Hopper and H200 AI platforms — NVIDIA Form 10‑Q (Q3 FY2025).
Cloud service providers accounted for roughly 50 % of Data Center revenue in Q3 FY2025, indicating heavy usage of NVIDIA GPUs for AI services — NVIDIA Form 10‑Q (Q3 FY2025).
NVIDIA announced shipments of the new Blackwell data‑center architecture beginning Q4 FY2025, expanding capacity for AI training clusters — NVIDIA Form 10‑Q (Q3 FY2025).
current.whyNow: In late October 2024 NVIDIA disclosed that demand for its upcoming Blackwell AI GPUs exceeds supply, prompting accelerated production ramps to meet surging AI model training needs.
risks: Exposure to U.S. export‑control restrictions that could limit sales of high‑performance GPUs to key markets such as China.
Supply‑chain constraints and long lead times for advanced semiconductor components that may impede the ability to meet growing AI demand.

sources.title: NVIDIA CORP Form 10-Q for the period ended October 27, 2024
